# Remember user preferences

Save volume and caption preferences, restore them after loading, and adapt the pattern for quality selection.

Save preferences from player state to local storage or your backend. Video.js leaves storage and per-profile settings to your application.

## Recommended approach

Subscribe to the state you want to remember, write it to storage when it changes, and restore it once the store attaches to the media.

**VolumePersistence.tsx**

```tsx
import { Container, createPlayer } from '@videojs/react';
import { Video, videoFeatures } from '@videojs/react/video';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

export const { Player, usePlayer } = createPlayer({ features: videoFeatures });

const STORAGE_KEY = 'player:volume';

// Guard storage access so playback still works when storage is blocked.
function readSaved(): { volume: number; muted: boolean } | null {
  try {
    const value = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) ?? 'null');

    return Number.isFinite(value?.volume) && typeof value?.muted === 'boolean' ? value : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function save(prefs: { volume: number; muted: boolean }) {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(prefs));
  } catch {
    // Storage unavailable; skip persistence.
  }
}

function VolumePersistence() {
  const store = usePlayer();
  const { volume, muted } = usePlayer((s) => ({ volume: s.volume, muted: s.muted }));
  // Read the saved value once, before the save effect below can write.
  const [saved] = useState(readSaved);
  const restored = useRef(false);

  // Save on change, once the restore has run.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!restored.current) return;

    save({ volume, muted });
  }, [volume, muted]);

  // Restore once the store attaches to the media; actions throw before that.
  useEffect(() => {
    const restore = () => {
      if (!store.target) return false;

      if (saved) {
        store.setVolume(saved.volume);

        // Apply saved mute after setVolume, which unmutes above zero.
        if (saved.muted) store.setMuted(true);
      }

      restored.current = true;
      return true;
    };
    if (restore()) return;

    const unsubscribe = store.subscribe(() => {
      if (restore()) unsubscribe();
    });

    return unsubscribe;
  }, [store, saved]);

  return null;
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Player>
      <Container>
        <Video src="https://stream.mux.com/BV3YZtogl89mg9VcNBhhnHm02Y34zI1nlMuMQfAbl3dM/highest.mp4" playsInline />
        <VolumePersistence />
      </Container>
    </Player>
  );
}
```

## How it works

- Player state is the single source of truth: it already reflects every change, whatever caused it — your UI, keyboard shortcuts, native controls, or scripts.
- `store.subscribe(callback)` fires on any state change. The store batches notifications per microtask, so changes made in the same tick produce one callback. There is no per-key subscription on the store: read the state and diff the slice you care about.
- `usePlayer(selector)` re-renders only when the selected value changes. To save a value, select it with `usePlayer` and write it to storage in an effect.
- Feature selectors exported by `@videojs/react` (`selectVolume`, `selectTextTrack`, `selectQuality`, and the rest) read a feature’s slice from any store, returning `undefined` when the feature isn’t present.
- Restore through the feature actions (`setVolume`, `setMuted`, `selectSubtitlesTrack`, `selectVideoRendition`) rather than poking the media component, so state and UI stay consistent.
- Actions need an attached media target: calling one before the store attaches throws. Check `store.target` and defer the restore until it is set, as the examples do.

## Availability and constraints

- Video.js does not write preferences to storage. Initial values come from the media component, track markup, and playback engine.
- `setVolume` clamps to 0–1 and unmutes above zero. Restore volume first, then call `setMuted(true)` if the saved preference is muted. Calling `setMuted(false)` at zero raises the volume to 0.25.
- The volume examples leave autoplay off. For muted autoplay, defer volume restoration until a user action: restoring a positive volume unmutes the media and can interrupt autoplay, even if you immediately mute it again.
- `setVolume` and `setMuted` update `store.state` immediately. A React hook’s selected value updates on the next render.
- Track and rendition lists arrive when the media loads, not when the player is created. Subscribe and restore a saved selection when its entry appears in the list.
- On iOS Safari, `volumeAvailability` is `'unsupported'` after attachment. Restoring the volume level has no effect there; mute can still be restored.
- Local storage is per-origin and can be unavailable (private modes, embedded contexts); guard reads and writes accordingly.

## Common variations

### Persist caption preference

Save the showing track’s `language` because track ids can change between sources. Save `'off'` when captions are off. Restore once when the first caption or subtitle list arrives, then save later selection changes. Do not wait for `canPlay`. With limited preloading, `canPlay` can stay `false` until playback starts. Repeated restoration would override a selection the user already made.

If the saved language is absent from that first list, leave the stored preference intact until the selection changes. This example does not retry restoration when more tracks arrive; adapt the initial loading step if your engine exposes languages in several batches. Browser selection changes after restoration are saved just like user changes.

`CaptionsPersistence` imports `usePlayer` from `VolumePersistence.tsx` above. Render `<CaptionsPersistence />` next to `<VolumePersistence />` inside `Container`. Add a `<track>` with `label` and `srcLang` for each language to `Video`, as in [Show captions and subtitles](./captions.md). Remount `CaptionsPersistence` when changing sources, using a key derived from the source URL, so restoration runs again.

Omit `default` from these tracks when persisting caption preferences. A default track can turn on after restoration, causing this example to save its language over a stored `'off'` preference.

**CaptionsPersistence.tsx**

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

import { usePlayer } from './VolumePersistence';

export default function CaptionsPersistence() {
  const store = usePlayer();
  const tracks = usePlayer((s) => s.textTrackList);
  const [saved] = useState(() => {
    try {
      return localStorage.getItem('player:captions');
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  });
  const restored = useRef(false);
  const lastSelection = useRef<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const subtitles = tracks.filter((t) => t.kind === 'captions' || t.kind === 'subtitles');
    if (!subtitles.length) return;

    const showing = subtitles.find((t) => t.mode === 'showing');
    const selection = showing ? showing.language : 'off';

    // Restore once the first subtitle list arrives, then honor later changes.
    if (!restored.current) {
      const desired = saved === 'off' ? undefined : subtitles.find((t) => t.language === saved);

      restored.current = true;
      lastSelection.current = selection;

      if (saved && (desired || saved === 'off')) {
        store.selectSubtitlesTrack(desired?.id ?? null);
      }

      return;
    }

    // Save only later selection changes, preserving an unmatched preference.
    if (selection === lastSelection.current) return;

    lastSelection.current = selection;

    try {
      localStorage.setItem('player:captions', selection);
    } catch {
      // Continue without persistence when storage is blocked.
    }
  }, [store, tracks, saved]);

  return null;
}
```

### Remember a quality selection

Adapt the same restore-then-save pattern to the [quality feature](../reference/api/feature-quality.md):

1. Save `'auto'` or the resolution of the selected entry in `videoRenditionList`. Read `selected`; `activeVideoRendition` can change during automatic playback and does not identify a manual preference.
2. Wait for the next source’s rendition list, then match the saved resolution to an entry. Rendition ids belong to that source, so do not reuse a saved id across sources.
3. Call `selectVideoRendition` with the matching entry’s id, or `'auto'` if no match exists. Every entry in `videoRenditionList` has an id; use it directly.
4. Do not save until restoration finishes; otherwise the source’s default selection overwrites the saved choice. After that, save each change the user makes.

To remember a data-saving limit while preserving automatic switching, persist `maxAutoResolution` and pass it on the next source. It needs the hls.js engine; native HLS playback ignores it. See [Options Video.js normalizes](./media-sources.md#options-videojs-normalizes).

### Persist to your backend

Swap `localStorage` for an API call; the subscription pattern is identical. Debounce writes beyond the built-in microtask batching if your storage is remote.

## Troubleshooting

### The saved volume doesn’t apply

Restore runs before the store attaches, or the platform doesn’t allow programmatic volume (check `volumeAvailability`). Apply after `store.target` is set, as in the examples.

### The saved caption track doesn’t select

The track list wasn’t loaded yet when you restored, or you saved a generated track id instead of a stable property like `language`. React to `textTrackList` changes and match on language.

### Storage writes fire constantly while dragging the volume slider

Notifications batch per microtask, but a drag still produces many ticks. Debounce the write if the churn matters for your storage target.
